test.name: cbtwrap
test.objective: A back-tab from the last column cancels the pending wrap.

iter.notes: KNOWN DEFECT in libghostty-vt (found by this suite, not yet reported upstream). Cursor backward tab (CBT, CSI Z) moves the cursor off the last column without clearing the pending wrap (Terminal.horizontalTabBack uses the raw screen cursorLeft), unlike CUB, CR, CHA and BS. The next character then lands one row below the cursor. Ghostty itself treats a pending wrap away from the last column as invalid (its snapshot decoder drops it), so a restored snapshot renders the same output differently.

result.verdict: back-tab kept the pending wrap: the next character went to the row below the cursor

test.name: chunking
test.objective: A terminal looks the same however its input is cut into writes.

iter.notes: KNOWN DEFECT in libvterm, the fallback backend: 0.1.4 (Debian 12, the image) and 0.3.3 (Ubuntu 24.04). A UTF-8 character cut between two writes after other text decodes as U+FFFD; the same bytes one at a time, or cut at the start of a line, decode correctly. Reproduced with libvterm alone (vterm_input_write), outside tsf-shell.

result.verdict: the terminal looks different when its input is fed one byte at a time
